one_liner: Diagnoses and treats illness — the person you see when something is wrong.
job_roles: General Physician | Surgeon | Paediatrician | Gynaecologist | Psychiatrist | Anaesthesiologist | Radiologist | Pathologist | Emergency Medicine Physician | Cardiologist
self_emp_route: Private practice or a clinic after registration, commonly alongside a hospital post.
ai_reason: Diagnostic support is improving fast and will change the work, but a registered human must examine, decide and carry liability. Physical examination and procedures are not text problems.
role_spread: [Psychiatrist, General Physician] higher: emotional_intelligence, verbal, agreeableness / lower: spatial, bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry, Biology AND English, with 50 percent in PCB -> entrance_exam: NEET UG. Minimum age 17, no upper age limit, no cap on attempts. -> degree: MBBS (4.5 years) at an NMC-recognised college -> internship: Compulsory 12-month rotating internship (CRMI) -> registration: Register with a State Medical Council — mandatory to practise -> specialisation: NEET PG then MD/MS for a specialist career (3 more years)
nuances: [economics] Cost is BIMODAL, not a range. A government seat costs roughly 1-5 lakh for the whole degree; a private or deemed seat costs 60 lakh to 1.2 crore. The figure shown is a blend and describes almost nobody. Which side of that line a student lands on is decided entirely by their NEET rank. || [class12_prerequisite] There is NO private bypass. Unlike engineering, money cannot open a door NEET has closed — the same eligibility applies to government, private and deemed colleges alike. || [entry_window] Null because NEET has no upper age limit and no cap on attempts. A commerce graduate is not permanently blocked — they can add PCB through NIOS and sit NEET at any age. It is a long cost, roughly 8 years, not a closed door. || [economics] The stored figure is a blend of two costs that are twenty times apart and it describes almost no real student. A government MBBS seat costs roughly 10,000-50,000 rupees a year - under 3 lakh for the whole degree, and as little as 6,000 a year at AIIMS Delhi. A private or deemed seat runs 15-25 lakh a year, 85 lakh to 1.3 crore for the course. Which one a student pays is decided entirely by their NEET rank, not by anything they can plan for.

one_liner: Treats teeth and gums — fillings, extractions, braces and oral surgery.
job_roles: General Dentist | Orthodontist | Endodontist | Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon | Periodontist | Prosthodontist | Paedodontist
self_emp_route: Own clinic, the normal destination in dentistry — a chair and a compressor are the capital.
ai_reason: Almost entirely manual work inside a patient's mouth, with a licensed human carrying liability. Treatment planning software is exposed; the hands are not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English with 50 percent in PCB -> entrance_exam: NEET UG -> degree: BDS (4 years) -> internship: Compulsory 1-year rotating internship -> registration: Register with a State Dental Council under the Dental Council of India
nuances: [demand_signal] Demand is real but graduate supply outruns it. India opens far more BDS seats than the market absorbs, so a large share of graduates end up underemployed or leave clinical work. This is an oversupply of dentists, not a fall in the need for dentistry - which is why the record stands with the demand tag unchanged rather than being dropped.

one_liner: Treats animals — pets, livestock and wildlife.
job_roles: Veterinary Surgeon | Livestock Veterinary Officer | Small Animal Practitioner | Veterinary Pathologist | Wildlife Veterinarian | Poultry & Dairy Health Officer
self_emp_route: Own small-animal clinic, or a livestock practice serving farms in a district.
ai_reason: Physical examination of animals that cannot describe symptoms, plus surgery and field work in livestock settings. A registered vet is legally accountable.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English -> entrance_exam: NEET UG for the all-India quota; state and ICAR entrances also apply -> degree: B.V.Sc & A.H. (5.5 years including internship) -> registration: Register with a State Veterinary Council under the Veterinary Council of India
nuances: [entrance_exams] ICAR AIEEA was listed here as an undergraduate route and that was wrong. AIEEA admits to MVSc at postgraduate level; the undergraduate BVSc door is NEET UG alone, the same examination and the same Physics-Chemistry-Biology-English subject set as MBBS. A student who wants to treat animals faces exactly the same gate as one who wants to treat people.

one_liner: Cares for patients around the clock — the person who is actually there.
job_roles: Staff Nurse | ICU / Critical Care Nurse | Operation Theatre Nurse | Paediatric Nurse | Community Health Nurse | Nurse Educator | Midwife
ai_reason: Overwhelmingly physical and present-tense — lifting, monitoring, administering, noticing a patient deteriorate before a monitor does. A registered nurse is legally accountable.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English -> entrance_exam: State nursing entrances or CUET; some states use NEET -> degree: B.Sc Nursing (4 years), or GNM diploma (3 years) -> registration: Register with a State Nursing Council and the Indian Nursing Council — mandatory to practise
nuances: [demand_signal] One of very few professions in this dataset where working abroad is a mainstream, well-established path rather than an exception. Gulf, UK and Ireland actively recruit Indian nurses, and pay differs several-fold. || [economics] Pay in this profession is bimodal and the stored band is a blend of the two. A government post sits on the 7th CPC matrix - AIIMS recruits Senior Nursing Officer / Staff Nurse Grade-I at Level 8, basic 47,600 to 1,51,100 rupees a month, before dearness and house rent allowance. A private hospital pays a fraction of that for the same work, and aggregate 'average salary' figures are dominated by private employment, which is why they read low. Which side a student lands on is decided by whether they clear a government recruitment examination, not by the qualification.

one_liner: First to reach an emergency — keeps people alive on the way to hospital.
job_roles: Emergency Medical Technician | Ambulance Paramedic | Advanced Life Support Technician | Emergency Room Technician | Disaster Response Medic
licensing_body: Trauma, Burn Care and Surgical/Anaesthesia Related Technology Professional Council (NCAHP)
ai_reason: Physical, unpredictable and time-critical. Decisions made in minutes with incomplete information at a roadside. Nothing about it is a text problem.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Science stream with Biology -> training: Certificate or B.Sc in Emergency Medical Technology (6 months to 3 years) -> certification: BLS and ACLS certification -> registration: Register under the NCAHP Act 2021
nuances: [economics] The lowest-paid profession in Sector 4 and the shortest to enter, and both facts matter together. It is a genuine destination - ambulance services, hospital emergency departments and industrial and event medical cover employ EMTs permanently - and it is also the most common bridge into nursing and other allied health courses, because the certificate stacks. The work is physically hard, done in shifts, and carries repeated exposure to trauma.

one_liner: Works on the health of whole populations, not one patient at a time.
job_roles: Epidemiologist | Public Health Officer | Programme Manager (health) | Health Policy Analyst | Disease Surveillance Officer | Community Health Specialist | Biostatistician (public health)
entrance_exams: CUET PG | Institute entrances (IIPH, AIIMS, TISS)
self_emp_route: Independent consulting to NGOs, foundations and government programmes.
ai_reason: Data analysis is exposed. Deciding which population question matters, and persuading a government to act on it, is not.
role_spread: [Epidemiologist, Biostatistician (public health)] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: extraversion, emotional_intelligence
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's — MBBS, BDS, nursing, life sciences, statistics and social sciences all feed in -> post_graduate: MPH (Master of Public Health) — this is the real entry qualification -> employment: Government health programmes, WHO and UN agencies, NGOs, research institutes
nuances: [mid_stream_entry] One of the most reachable healthcare careers for a non-PCB student. The MPH accepts graduates from statistics, social sciences and management — no NEET, no biology at class 12, no clinical degree required.
